03 / How I work

Five steps.
No surprises at the end.

You sign off after the script, the storyboard and the style frames, so the look and every claim are agreed before animation starts.

  1. 01

    Script

    I research your device and write from your IFU, FDA summary or approved copy. Every claim is listed with its source, ready for your MLR or regulatory review.

  2. 02

    Storyboard

    Every shot planned with timing, camera moves and on-screen text. Changes here take minutes, not days.

  3. 03

    Style frames

    Two or three finished stills in your brand, so you approve the exact look before anything moves.

  4. 04

    Animation

    Motion design, device shots, voiceover and music. Each shot is checked against your product photos and the anatomy.

  5. 05

    Final

    A 1080p master, plus the cutdowns and loops you ordered. Two rounds of changes on the cut are included.

05 / Questions

Good to know

Were these films made for these companies?

No. They are spec concepts I made on my own to show the craft, using only claims from each company's public pages or the FDA record. None of the companies commissioned, reviewed or endorsed them.

Do you use AI?

Yes, as one tool among many. Some scenes start as AI-generated footage. Every take is checked against the real device and the anatomy, and thrown out if it's wrong. The script, the claims, the motion graphics and the edit are made by me.

What do you need from us to start?

Product photos or renders, your brand guidelines and your approved claims (an IFU, an FDA summary or existing marketing copy). If you have none of these yet, I start from your public website and the FDA record.

How long does a film take?

Most 45–60 second films take two to three weeks, depending mainly on how quickly approvals come back.

Where are you based?

Sri Lanka (GMT+5:30). Feedback you send at the end of your working day is often answered by your next morning.
